text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

--The Danish government is working on legislation to ban motorcycle gangs in Denmark. The public prosecutor and minister of justice are investigating legal and constitutional aspects of a ban, which could be in place by the end of the year. The Nordic region is the scene of an ever-escalating turf war between rival Bandidos and Hells Angels bikers, the latest episode being a shooting in early June which left one Danish Bandidos dead and three wounded.

--A majority in the political leadership of the far-left Socialist Peoples Party supports the results the Social Democrat-led government achieved in the Amsterdam EU summit, pointing to a likely recommendation by the party to its members to vote "yes" in Denmark's referendum on EU reforms to be held at an as yet unspecified date in 1998.

--The Danish government seems to be losing control of public sector expenditure with new data from the national statistics office showing that public spending rose by 2.4 percent in 1996 to 627 billion crowns. The data cast doubt on the credibility of government fiscal policy, an economist at leading Den Danske Bank said.

--According to government report, there are around one million Danes receiving state benefits of one kind or the other out of a population of just over five million. Unveiling the study, economy ministerr Marianne Jelved criticised local authorities in Denmark for sending too many people on state-financed early retirement.
